study.question: After preserving match-count, aligned-age and action-support evidence, does one mixed history vector still discard useful action-specific content, and does learned target-aware weighting add value to separately pooled action content?
study.hypothesis: Provisional mechanism: retaining four separately normalized action summaries preserves content otherwise compressed into the incumbent mixed vector. Source inspection confirms the current single global softmax and summed category/brand/action/age event embeddings. r0000-match_count exceeds support_count by 0.00343557 AUC; match_rate exceeds support_rate by 0.00342757, suggesting target relevance beyond activity. r0001-aligned_time exceeds duplicate_count by 0.00051789 and factorized_time by 0.00088953, suggesting useful event-aligned recency in this seed. However r0002-joint_pair (0.61835222) does not beat factorized_pair (0.61837420), and support_pair (0.61845667, logloss 0.19599073) is the incumbent. Duplicate_pair itself reaches 0.61801300 versus its smaller parent 0.61714903, warning that readout shape and initialization matter. First-512 candidate-supplied diagnostics show mean pair-valid action counts pv 111.6621/cart 3.1914/fav 1.2695/buy 1.9922 (pv 94.54% of summed counts); this is not a population composition estimate or evidence of learned attention suppression. Full validation includes cart-present 2111110, fav-present 1179004, buy-present 1888339 impressions, so action-specific information is available broadly. These observations motivate a controlled test; they do not establish the pooling mechanism. All 15 available trials succeeded; no failed execution is supplied, and previous_runtime_error is null.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/1706.06978v4 ; DIN v4, section 4.3, equation 3, inspected in this context
nearest_work.difference: Inherits target-versus-history local activation. The supplied reference uses normalized softmax unlike original DIN, which explicitly removes normalization. Retain the supplied variant unchanged as the base; append action-specific normalized summaries. Neither a faithful DIN reproduction nor a claim to invent target attention.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/2104.06312v1 ; EDIN/DINMP v1 sections 3.1.2-3 and 3.2.1-2, inspected in this context
nearest_work.difference: Prior work aggregates weighted behavior embeddings by time/category partitions and feeds aggregate vectors onward. Here partition only the frozen supplied 128 events by four action IDs, with one shared scorer, separate masked softmax and fixed existing count/decay/support evidence. No sparse-key acquisition, long-history extension, extra partition interaction layer or source split is adopted. Grouped pooling is inherited prior art; novelty remains unverified.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://aisel.aisnet.org/amcis2023/sig_dsa/sig_dsa/6/ ; Jin et al. 2023, Advertising Click-Through Rate Prediction Based on Multi-Behavior Sequences, primary abstract
nearest_work.difference: Primary abstract explicitly proposes DMBIN multi-behavior hierarchical attention, so multi-behavior attention is not new. Download https://aisel.aisnet.org/cgi/viewcontent.cgi?article=1184&context=amcis2023 returned 403; architecture and detailed equivalence remain unverified. Current design only appends shared-scorer action summaries with a two-factor control suite, without claiming a new architecture family.

nearest_work.source_ref: https://arxiv.org/html/1711.06632 ; ATRank v2, introduction and framework overview, inspected in this context
nearest_work.difference: Heterogeneous behavior attention predates this experiment. We retain the supplied event embedding rather than introducing multi-space projections, self-attention or extra supervision. This is a restricted low-cost adaptation with explicit action pooling controls, not an ATRank reproduction.

study.proposed_difference: Append four 16-dimensional vectors after all existing parent inputs, increasing the first MLP layer by 64*128=8192 parameters (expected total 17141539, dense 62851, embeddings 17078688). Factor A is separately normalized action pools (pv/cart/fav/buy order) versus four identical copies of a global pool. Factor B is learned target-aware score weighting versus uniform averaging. Always retain the incumbent global learned-attention vector, including in mean controls, so the scorer remains active and trained. All four variants have the same modules, initialization sequence and forward view calculations. Use batched matrix products for action pooling without constructing [B,4,L,D] values. No extra query/scorer, labels, optimizer/loss change or data selection. Empty action groups produce exact zero, missing field IDs retain existing masking in fixed statistics. Grouped learned pooling is a mechanism-distinct local candidate relative to adding deterministic match/support scalars, but not verified novel in the literature.
predictions: Primary contrast: action_attention AUC exceeds global_attention (duplicated global learned pool) at identical shapes and recipe. Candidate also should exceed the narrower incumbent for deployment value; that unmatched comparison alone provides no attribution.

Factorial contrasts: action_mean - global_mean measures grouping under uniform weights; action_attention - action_mean and global_attention - global_mean measure weighting within each grouping. Positive interaction (AUC_action_attention - AUC_global_attention) - (AUC_action_mean - AUC_global_mean) supports incremental learned weighting with grouping. A positive action main effect without interaction supports grouping only.

Exploratory action-present/absent slices use existing host definitions and must retain each sample/positive/negative count. Compare cart/fav/buy presence strata but do not treat overlapping strata as independent or infer mechanism from different baseline AUCs. Empty histories and sparse actions may fail to benefit.

First-512 diagnostics will report action counts, conditional global attention mass, conditional uniform mass, within-action attention effective support, norms and attention-versus-mean vector distance. Low global action mass with measurable changed action content is consistent with a competition bottleneck, not proof. Empty and padding masks must yield zero absent summaries and finite scalars.
falsifiers: If action_attention fails to beat the matched global_attention control, the proposed implementation lacks support even if both exceed the narrower parent.

If action_mean matches or exceeds action_attention and the factorial interaction is nonpositive, learned target-aware weighting specific to grouping is unsupported; any useful result is attributed to grouping or optimization pending repetitions.
If duplicate global summaries improve as much as grouped ones, a larger readout or different initialization is sufficient as an alternative explanation.

If reported attention is already concentrated on rare actions or action/mean vectors differ negligibly, suppression is not supported by these descriptive diagnostics. One failed pooling implementation does not refute all action-conditioned models.

If candidate costs exceed the trial cap, outputs are nonfinite, or input/parameter controls fail, record an execution or integrity failure; do not reinterpret it as scientific counterevidence or enlarge the cap.
alternative_explanations: Action grouping simultaneously exposes separate action content and changes the normalization population; this suite cannot isolate those two aspects.
Equal allocated parameters do not imply equal effective function rank: repeated vectors are intentionally redundant.
All views are computed in every forward, but only selected views backpropagate; equal measured compute is not assumed.
Seed 42 search results and first-512-row diagnostics are preliminary; attention mass is not causal importance.
Action support and recency statistics may already capture all useful behavior differences; separate learned content could add noise.
Separate rare-action normalization may amplify irrelevant singleton events, especially when category and brand are coarse or missing.
Present/absent slice differences reflect user activity and exposure frequency; they do not demonstrate a causal behavior effect.
Shared score attention cancels any constant per-action score offset within each action pool; training dynamics can change even with fixed scorer capacity.
Validation-adaptive selection across rounds, static snapshots with unknown as-of dates, and one-seed variation limit generalization. No test feedback is available or used.

cost_plan.attribution_reserve: Keep at least 7043.73 seconds beyond the current four calls for up to four capped discriminating follow-ups, including failures. Forward views are shared across modes; backward cost differs. Report actual total/dense/embedding parameters, training and allocated GPU seconds when exposed, examples, wall, peak memory, throughput and batch p50/p95 latency. Same data passes isolate mechanism; efficiency claims require measured costs, not estimated equality.
cost_plan.assessment_reserve: Reserve at least 15848.40 seconds for up to nine capped validation-only runs: three paired seeds 42/43/44 for the selected candidate and two closest controls. If a four-way interaction remains consequential, reserve another three capped runs (5282.80 seconds) for all four cells across three seeds; total interaction assessment reserve 21131.20. Freeze source/config/checkpoint suite and assessment commands before any final assessment. No test outcomes or predictions are authorized. This proposal does not execute assessment.
cost_plan.stop_rule: Never exceed host remaining budget or per-trial cap. Stop this phase after four registered variants and local syntax/source/scalar checks; no local training or installation. Keep attribution plus interaction-assessment reserve (28174.93 seconds) intact. If a useful follow-up does not fit, retain null/negative evidence and stop. An unavailable Torch/data runtime is missing execution capability, not a failed scientific result.
